stage: Independent inspection saved before opening frozen brief or judge aesthetic criteria
originalObservations: The sofa reads as a wide three-seat rose and tan object, with a continuous high back, separate back pillows, long low seat pads, arms, brown base and tiny feet.
Large surfaces are planar chamfered slabs; faces become dark abruptly and upholstery has little compression or softness.
Damage is represented by a small brown rectangle with tan inset and a thin blue diagonal bar. It is readable as markings, but not as a substantial tear, tuft or repair.
Two foreground loose blocks appear separated from the body; groundedness needs native measurement rather than image guessing.
targetObservations: The target keeps the three-seat rose sofa and cream center cushion while making the arms and back cushions fuller and more rounded.
Warm peach upper light, muted red-purple lower upholstery and an amber structural rail separate materials without a hard planar dark band.
Thin perimeter seams, visible sag, a stitched left patch, restrained stains and cream stuffing emerging from jagged openings provide useful worn identity.
The target fills much more of its canvas, so its image scale cannot be copied over the registered native capture. Its dimensional, upholstered construction is the transferable goal.
styleReferenceObservations: The reference uses a bright warm rim on thick edges, broad uncluttered color regions and soft shaded depth. It remains a concise cartoon form.
nativeObservations: The library contains twenty direct mesh roles under garbage-sofa__root, plus sixty named baked native actions, with no armature.
The source has semantic independent base, four feet, back, two arms, three seats, three back pillows, fabric, stuffing, spring and three debris roles.
All primary upholstery is cube-based beveled geometry. This allows native curvature, seams, compressed cushions and actual repair construction without preserving the old mesh count.
The saved active camera is S33 Capture Camera.240; it is not sufficient evidence for the sofa's capture. Use the sofa camera record and project calibration.
Initial raw object bounds were inspected before forcing dependency-graph update; the inspection records local construction dimensions but is not the final world-envelope audit.
